name: Vettel
workload: Adding 1000 keys to the store, wall-clock time measured with shell `time` for both vettel and a Redis client script
claimed_speedup: 1.24x faster (10.72s vettel vs 13.26s redis, wall time for 1000 inserts)
hardware: author's 'mid-2012 MacBook Pro' (exact CPU model not stated)
tradeoffs: ~300 lines of C, minimal command set, single-threaded, no documented persistence/consistency guarantees; toy-scale project
caveats: Margin is small (1.24x) and could be noise; hardware is a 2012-era laptop with no CPU model or compiler flags given; benchmark scripts are bundled but not independently reproduced
found_via: Hacker News: 'key-value store faster than Redis' -> Show HN: Vettel - a tiny key value store that's faster than Redis (sort of) (2023-02-12, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=34760870)

name: warp_cache
workload: Python @cache() decorator get/set ops/s, single- and multi-threaded, Zipf-distributed keys (2000 unique), cache size 256, Python 3.13.2
claimed_speedup: ~25x faster than cachetools single-threaded (20.4M vs 826K ops/s); ~26x multi-threaded at 16 threads (19.5M vs 795K ops/s); also 1.6x faster than functools.lru_cache+Lock under multithreading
hardware: Apple M-series (arm64), exact chip model not stated
tradeoffs: Single-threaded functools.lru_cache (pure C, no FFI) is itself ~1.5x faster than warp_cache; warp_cache's win only materializes once thread-safety is required; adds a Rust/PyO3 build dependency
caveats: First-party benchmark in the project's own repo; CPU given only as 'Apple M-series', not an exact model; not independently reproduced
found_via: Hacker News: 'Show HN cache faster' -> Show HN: Warp_cache - SIEVE cache in Rust for Python, 25x faster than cachetools (2026-03-08, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47301973)

name: Yac (PHP shared-memory object cache)
workload: Full WordPress homepage renders under `ab -t 30 -c <concurrency>` at 20/50/100 concurrent users, PHP 8.1 FPM, 8 cores, comparing the Yac object-cache drop-in vs the classic Memcached drop-in on the author's live site (laruence.com)
claimed_speedup: +18.6% to +20.1% RPS (e.g. 142.1 vs 118.4 RPS at c=100) and ~15-19% lower p50 latency (699ms vs 840ms at c=100); cross-checked with a fixed-count run (ab -n 10000 -c 100): +17.6% RPS
hardware: 8-core server running PHP 8.1 FPM; exact CPU model not stated
stars_or_usage: 833 stars (yac core extension); 5 stars (wp-yac-cache WordPress plugin)
tradeoffs: Only benefits single-node or few-node installs where PHP workers share a machine (no cross-node cache the way Memcached/Redis provide); shared-memory segment is capacity-bounded; keys over Yac's 48-byte limit get hashed instead of stored verbatim
caveats: Real-site benchmark from the plugin author's own blog/repo, not independently reproduced; hardware stated only as '8 cores', no exact CPU model or compiler flags; single-site sample; the HN-quoted '~19% faster' figure is the throughput/latency number, while the plugin listing separately claims a much larger 170x-730x gain for raw round-trip time which this entry does not use because no methodology was given for that figure
found_via: Hacker News: 'faster than memcached' -> WordPress object cache backed by shared memory, ~19% faster than Memcached (2026-09-13, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49680028)

name: Ferrous
workload: Standardized redis-benchmark testing of core RESP commands (PING, SET, etc.) and pipelined operations, Ferrous vs Valkey 8.0.4
claimed_speedup: Ferrous ~5-8% faster than Valkey on single-command ops; PING pipeline +25% (833k vs 667k ops/s); but SET pipeline is 94% faster on Valkey's side (588k vs 303k ops/s) - a mixed, not uniform, win
tradeoffs: No Redis module system, clustering incomplete; README states the project was developed entirely through AI-assisted programming; SET pipelining is notably slower than Valkey
caveats: Results are mixed (wins on some ops, loses badly -94% on SET pipelining); compared against Valkey (a Redis fork), not upstream Redis, so baseline_in_list=false; no hardware/compiler/flags stated; the HN submission title 'Outperforms Valkey' overstates the README's own mixed table
found_via: Hacker News: 'outperforms Redis' -> Ferrous: Redis-Compatible Server in Rust That Outperforms Valkey (2025-08-08, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44838206)
